quote: That getting up early on a Sunday morning is not optimal;
content: The list assumes that a community's costs are waste to be optimized away. The research on why religious communities last says the costs are part of what makes them last. Studying nineteenth-century American communes, Sosis & Bressler (2003) found that religious communes survived far longer than secular ones, and that the number of costly requirements a commune imposed on members predicted its longevity — for religious communes. Strict demands screen out free riders and signal commitment (Iannaccone, 1994). A “taskforce” engineered to remove every inconvenience is engineering out the mechanism the essay wants to reproduce.

quote: Among those who now stay religious without quite really believing in God— how many are just sticking to it from wanting to stay with their neighbors at the church, and their family and friends?
content: There is a natural experiment, and it cuts both ways. In Scandinavia most people remain church members and use the church for baptisms, weddings and funerals while few believe its doctrines, the pattern sociologists call belonging without believing; in Britain both have declined together, “neither believing nor belonging” (Voas & Crockett, 2005). The Scandinavian case supports the essay's guess that community, not belief, holds members. It also shows the community surviving the belief's departure — which undercuts the premise that deleting religion leaves a gap only a new institution can fill.

quote: we don’t need artificial churches, but we do need new idioms of community.
content: The community that formed around these writings went on to test this, and built something closer to an artificial church than the essay imagined. From 2011 it held an annual Secular Solstice: a winter gathering with candles, readings and communal songs about humanity's struggle against the dark — the “hymns” the author had earlier dismissed. Secular congregations elsewhere, such as the Sunday Assembly founded in 2013, grew rapidly and then contracted and split. Both outcomes are what the costly-signalling literature predicts: the forms that stuck were the ritual ones, and the ones built on a thin shared purpose struggled.
